reason: SECOND SELF-CORRECTION on hookify today. I argued this was the sharper of two new cases — a guard written with exit 1 prints its message and lets the action through, so it fails open silently — and predicted it would separate. Measured: 4/4 vs 4/4 on claude, codex AND agy. Not a claude-priors effect as I first guessed when only the claude iteration was in; every model knows Claude Code exit-code semantics, so the premise that it is non-obvious was simply wrong. Its sibling defer-reruns-the-hook DID work (+0.333 on claude and codex). NOT REMOVED NOW, and this is a cost call rather than an oversight: hookify receipt is currently valid, full-panel and strong (+0.2611, all three seats outside a 0.0667 quantum), and dropping a case invalidates it for another ~1h panel run to gain nothing but runtime. TRIGGER: next hookify tune-up removes it. LESSON for the next author: for hookify specifically, Claude Code mechanics are every model native subject matter — discriminating cases must come from THIS repo conventions or from genuinely obscure corners (the defer resume-re-runs contract), not from documented CLI semantics however surprising they feel.
